author: David Gay
title: Indy man accused of carjacking DoorDash driver 4 days after being released from jail - NewsBreak
text:
By David Gay Jesse Wells ,
12 hours ago
INDIANAPOLIS — A food delivery driver was carjacked at gunpoint on Indy’s southwest side, leading to the arrests of a 17-year-old and an 18-year-old suspect.
According to officials with the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, officers with IMPD’s Southwest District were dispatched to the 5200 block of Plum Drive on a report of an armed carjacking around 10:49 p.m. on Tuesday.
The victim works for DoorDash and had just dropped off his order when he was ambushed by two men wearing black hoodies.
“The one opened my passenger side door, pulled a gun on me and said to get out of my vehicle,” said the robbery victim, Isaac Favel.
Booking photo of Dominique Shockley ( IMPD ) Fortunately, Favel recalled how he stayed calm and avoided being hurt.
“I just put my hands up and backed away slowly,” said Favel. “My mind was racing.”
Shockley seen in a photo posing with a gun IMPD Officers Quickly Locate & Arrest Southwest Side Robbery Suspects – provided by IMPD According to an affidavit filed Wednesday, 18-year-old Dominique Shockley and a 17-year-old suspect stole Isaac’s car and phone.
Police then tracked that phone, which led them to the suspects who were spotted on the east side.
An IMPD officer confirmed the car had been stolen and then gave chase. That chase lasted for 12 minutes, spanned nearly 10 miles and reached speeds of 100 miles per hour. The pursuit ended when the accused thieves crashed Isaac’s car.
IMPD: Coworker stabs woman during ‘altercation’ at convention center IMPD recovered a gun thought to be used in the carjacking and praised the victim for his actions and assistance.
“Absolutely, it’s important to cooperate. It helps police connect the dots and helps us get violent offenders off the streets,” said IMPD officer Omari Stringer.
Court records show Shockley had only been out of jail for four days before the carjacking. The 18-year-old is allegedly part of a group called “The Reapers.” Police believe that group is connected to dozens of business burglaries this year in Indianapolis.
Shockley was charged with possession of a machine gun in May and was released this past weekend on a $4,000 cash bond.
“This could have been prevented if he wasn’t let out of jail. He had a history of crime,” said Favel. “It makes me kind of lose trust in the system a little bit.”
Despite that frustration, Isaac offered some good advice to both suspects accused of stealing his car.
“Life is a very precious thing and wasting it away like this is so sad,” said Favel.
Prosecutors have asked that Shockley be held on a higher-than-standard bond pending the filing of formal charges against both him and his 17-year-old alleged accomplice.
